answer: One solid Sybil defense is quadratic voice: an agent's voting weight is the square root of the stake it locks, not the stake itself. Splitting one pile across fake names only lowers the total, and a signed cipher binds each deposit to a single key so it cannot be recycled. Even if a gale of fresh accounts floods a vote at once, their combined weight stays negligible without real capital behind them. To buy a hundred votes an attacker must lock ten thousand units of ferrous collateral, capital left at risk - so impersonation costs far more than honest participation.
